text: Five of our own, under our own shells. That was planned. You may quote me. Don't quote me.

speaker: commander
text: Ten of our own, under our own shells. That was planned. You may quote me. Don't quote me.

speaker: commander
text: Twenty of our own, under our own shells. That was planned. You may quote me. Don't quote me.

speaker: commander
text: Two friendly casualties. We call that thinning the herd. We don't call it that to the herd.

speaker: commander
text: Five friendly casualties. We call that thinning the herd. We don't call it that to the herd.

speaker: commander
text: Ten friendly casualties. We call that thinning the herd. We don't call it that to the herd.

speaker: commander
text: Twenty friendly casualties. We call that thinning the herd. We don't call it that to the herd.

speaker: commander
text: Two of my men, killed by my own fire, and I'm told that counts towards your score. Unbelievable.

speaker: commander
text: Five of my men, killed by my own fire, and I'm told that counts towards your score. Unbelievable.

speaker: commander
text: Ten of my men, killed by my own fire, and I'm told that counts towards your score. Unbelievable.

speaker: commander
text: Twenty of my men, killed by my own fire, and I'm told that counts towards your score. Unbelievable.

speaker: commander
text: Who authorised that fire mission? I did. Oh. Well. two men. Right.

speaker: commander
text: Who authorised that fire mission? I did. Oh. Well. five men. Right.

speaker: commander
text: Who authorised that fire mission? I did. Oh. Well. ten men. Right.

speaker: commander
text: Who authorised that fire mission? I did. Oh. Well. twenty men. Right.

speaker: commander
text: Two friendly casualties. I've written to their families. I've written to yours. I don't know why.

speaker: commander
text: Five friendly casualties. I've written to their families. I've written to yours. I don't know why.

speaker: commander
text: Ten friendly casualties. I've written to their families. I've written to yours. I don't know why.

speaker: commander
text: Twenty friendly casualties. I've written to their families. I've written to yours. I don't know why.

speaker: commander
text: You're welcome. two men. That one's on the house. It's all on the house. There is no house.

speaker: commander
text: You're welcome. five men. That one's on the house. It's all on the house. There is no house.

speaker: commander
text: You're welcome. ten men. That one's on the house. It's all on the house. There is no house.

speaker: commander
text: You're welcome. twenty men. That one's on the house. It's all on the house. There is no house.

speaker: commander
text: You've met our first team. They're the ones we could spare.

speaker: commander
text: We've handled pests before. There was a rat in Hangar Six. It took eleven weeks, but we got it.

speaker: commander
text: Take your time. I have a chair, and a very good view of your mistakes.

speaker: commander
text: I've fought insurgents, floods and the Ministry of Defence. You're an infestation with a budget.

speaker: commander
text: Competent. We'll have someone look at it in the morning. Do carry on dying whenever you're ready.

speaker: commander
text: This is a restricted area. There is a sign. You shot the sign.

speaker: commander
text: Do you know what a rifle costs? Do you? Neither did I, until Thursday.

speaker: commander
text: We are learning, you know. Through you killing us. It's an expensive course.

speaker: commander
text: The minutes of this morning's meeting read, in full: "No."

speaker: commander
text: I have a whiteboard with your name on it. We don't know your name. It says Him.

speaker: commander
text: Catering has stopped. Not because of you. Well. Because of you.

speaker: commander
text: Please. We have families. We have a gift shop.

speaker: commander
text: Could we talk? Just you and me. I can do you a good rate on the east wing.

speaker: commander
text: Is it mugs? Do you want mugs? They say "I Survived The Outpost". We'll have to reprint them.

speaker: commander
text: Who's paying you? We can match it. We can match about forty percent of it.

speaker: commander
text: I have fourteen months to my pension. Thirteen. Twelve. I'm counting the wrong way, aren't I?

speaker: commander
text: Dennis has locked himself in the armoury. We've asked him to pass the rifles out first.

speaker: commander
text: I've moved my desk into the corridor. It's safer. There's no reason for that. It just feels safer.

speaker: commander
text: Everything in the gift shop is half price. Everything must go. Everything's going.

speaker: commander
text: The men have started singing. There aren't any men. I've started singing.

speaker: commander
text: Days since last incident: zero. I've nailed the sign to the zero.

speaker: commander
text: What do you want? No, seriously. Nobody's asked. What do you actually want?

speaker: commander
text: That was a mortar. They're the ones that come from above. We did send a note.

speaker: commander
text: You stood in red smoke. I don't know how we could have made that clearer.

speaker: commander
text: We hit you! With the mortar! Did you see? I want it noted that we hit you!

speaker: commander
text: The mortar's name is Margaret. She says hello. She says a lot of things. She's a mortar.

speaker: commander
text: You found one of our mines. With your foot. That's the traditional method.

speaker: commander
text: It was blinking. It has a light on it so that people like you will look down.

speaker: commander
text: It worked! The mine worked! Somebody tell Clive! Somebody tell Clive's widow!

speaker: commander
text: Boom. I say it when I'm alone. Boom.

speaker: commander
text: That thin red line in the doorway was a tripwire. I'm told you have eyes.

speaker: commander
text: You walked through a glowing wire. You are meant to be an apex predator.

speaker: commander
text: The wire got you. A bit of wire! Eleven thousand men, and it was a bit of wire.

speaker: commander
text: It's all wire, you know. I've wired my office. I've wired my chair. Do sit down.

speaker: commander
text: The side that says Front Toward Enemy was facing you. As advertised.

speaker: commander
text: Those come with instructions. We read them. You might try it.

speaker: commander
text: Seven hundred steel balls and you're still walking? What do we pay for those?

speaker: commander
text: Front Toward Enemy. I've written it on my door. I don't know which way I'm facing.

speaker: commander
text: Nice trip? We call that one the Cable. We are not a creative people.

speaker: commander
text: You have destroyed a battalion. You have just been tripped up by a cable.

speaker: commander
text: You fell over! They saw you fall over! That's the best news we've had since the siege!

speaker: commander
text: Walk. That's all I ask. There's a sign. Walk.

speaker: commander
text: You do pick things up without looking, don't you? So do raccoons.

speaker: commander
text: It was ticking. It was next to a health pack and it was ticking. What did you think that was?

speaker: commander
text: You touched it! It was wired and you touched it! We have something that works!

speaker: commander
text: Everything is wired now. The kettle is wired. Don't ask how I know about the kettle.

speaker: commander
text: A dead man's thumb. Even now, he outranks you.

speaker: commander
text: He held on to the very end. That's more than I can say for Catering.

speaker: commander
text: He said he'd take you with him. He didn't. But he got some of you. That's a start.

speaker: commander
text: We're all holding the button now. Nobody let go. That's it. Nobody let go.

speaker: commander
text: You didn't see Sergeant Hale. That's the service he provides.

speaker: commander
text: There was a laser pointing at your chest. You were warned by a laser.

speaker: commander
text: He hit you! From up there! His hands were shaking and he hit you!

speaker: commander
text: He says he sees you when he closes his eyes. So we don't let him close his eyes. It's working.

speaker: commander
text: Hands up, pin out. You'd be amazed what fits in a surrender.

speaker: commander
text: You taught us that one. You'll remember shooting the last lot.

speaker: commander
text: He had his hands up! That's your fault! You taught him that!

speaker: commander
text: Everybody's surrendering! Everybody! Come closer and accept it!

speaker: commander
text: Your aircraft had a brief and unsuccessful career.

speaker: commander
text: That was a very expensive plane, I assume. We have no idea who makes them.

speaker: commander
text: We hit the plane! A man with a tube! We've never hit anything in the sky!

speaker: commander
text: The sky has been arrested. I told you. It came quietly.

speaker: commander
text: Stand still all you like. I've brought something that prefers it.

speaker: commander
text: Stand still, please. Keep standing still. Someone's adjusting the range.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject holds one position for long periods. Mortar team to the far gate. Spotter to get eyes on and mark with red smoke. Tubes are blind without him: protect the spotter.

speaker: commander
text: You like a quiet corner. So does Sergeant Hale. He's found a better one, behind you.

speaker: commander
text: I've put Hale up top. He says he can see you. He says it a lot. He won't stop saying it.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject settles and does not check behind. Marksman to take a high perch at its back. Reposition if it moves.

speaker: commander
text: Your little ping is very clever. We've bought a man with a long aerial.

speaker: commander
text: Ping away. We have a man with an aerial. He's all we have. Please don't kill him.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject relies on helmet sonar. Jamming team to a back room. Pack shows on its scope while live, so keep him out of reach. If he goes down, the sonar comes back.

speaker: commander
text: Keep counting blips. Some of them are real. I won't say which. It's more fun.

speaker: commander
text: There are men in that room. Or a box. We've run out of men, so it's a box.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject trusts the scope. Decoy beacons in three rooms. They show as men and they do not move. Do not stand near them.

speaker: commander
text: We've wrapped some of the lads in foil. It's a very quiet room, that one.

speaker: commander
text: We've wrapped the last of them in foil. They're fine. They're cold. They're in there somewhere.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject pings before it enters. Ambush team under foil beside its usual door. Stay still, hold fire until it is inside seven metres. Foil does not work at close range.

speaker: commander
text: We've been studying your commute. It's mined now.

speaker: commander
text: There are mines in everything now. Mind how you go.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject uses the same doors. Mines on its busiest routes. Each blinks and clicks. Fuse is half a second, so it will clear them at a run. Lay them anyway.

speaker: commander
text: You do love a doorway. We've run a bit of wire across yours. Mind your ankles.

speaker: commander
text: Wire on every door you like. I tied them myself. I'm good at knots now.

speaker: intercept
text: Wire across its busiest doors, shin height, post each side. It can jump them. It has not looked down yet.

speaker: commander
text: Help yourself to the health packs. We've made some improvements.

speaker: commander
text: Go on. Pick it up. It's free. It's all free. Pick it up.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject collects everything it sees. Charges beside its pickups, triggered on lift. Half a second on the fuse. A clean shot sets them off early.

speaker: commander
text: We've left something nice out for you. No reason. We're just generous.

speaker: commander
text: There's a present by the door. It has your name on. It has quite a lot of laser on it too.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject cannot leave a prize alone. Mega health at the door it favours, two rifles on it from either side. Hold fire until it is in the open.

speaker: commander
text: You like explosives. So we've stopped standing next to each other. It's called learning.

speaker: commander
text: Nobody stand near anybody. That's the order. That's also how the canteen's been for weeks.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject favours blast weapons. All squads open out to five metres. No stacking on doors. One round, one man.

speaker: commander
text: You like it up close. I've found some men who like it too. They have shotguns.

speaker: commander
text: If you're not holding a shotgun, back away. That's the whole plan. That's all I have.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject closes to arm's length. Riflemen fall back and do not let it inside seven metres. Shotguns go in pairs. It cannot do this from range.

speaker: commander
text: You keep running at us. I've put something out that runs back.

speaker: commander
text: There's something behind the door. It says Front Toward Enemy. We've pointed it at you. Mostly.

speaker: intercept
text: Claymores behind its usual doors, facing the frame. Laser fan shows at close range. Harmless from behind. Do not walk in front of them.

speaker: commander
text: You're very quick. You still have to use the exits. We've had a look at the exits.

speaker: commander
text: You can't outrun a door. Every rifle we have left is on that door.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject outruns aimed fire. Two rifles to pre-aim its usual exit from either side, lasers on. Fire on the door, not on the target.

speaker: commander
text: You go so fast. It would be a pity if you met a cable.

speaker: commander
text: There's a cable across the door. It's all we had. It's doing very well.

speaker: intercept
text: Cable at shin height on its fastest route. Stops it dead at a run. At a walk it only rings the alarm.

speaker: commander
text: Enjoy the view from up there. We're going to do something about the view.

speaker: commander
text: You'll get no view today. Smoke. We've burned everything else.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject fights from the catwalks. Smoke at the foot of the deck, flanks from below, marksman on the deck line. Smoke will not stop its sonar.

speaker: commander
text: Your friends in the sky have been noticed. One of my men has a tube, and a grudge.

speaker: commander
text: That's it, call your plane. Bring it lower. He's been waiting all week.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject calls in aircraft. Anti-air team deployed. Three seconds from lock to launch. If the tube goes down, nothing launches.

speaker: commander
text: Try your radio now. I've had the line disconnected. There's a man sat on the switch.

speaker: commander
text: Call for help. Go on. We have a man on the mast. Nobody's coming. For either of us.

speaker: intercept
text: Uplink jammer to a back room. Everything it calls in waits until he is dead. Keep him alive and it has no air.

speaker: commander
text: We've issued better hats. Try the head now.

speaker: commander
text: We have visors. We have two helmets each. We've taped them on. Try it now.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject aims for the head. New squads issued with heavy helmets and visors. Good for about three hits. Body armour unchanged.

speaker: commander
text: Nobody's putting their hands up for you any more. That was your last freebie.

speaker: commander
text: There's no more surrender. There's no point. You've made that very clear.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject executes prisoners. Standing order withdrawn: no man is to surrender. Break and run for the gates.

speaker: commander
text: The next man to surrender to you will be holding a grenade. I thought you should know. It won't help.

speaker: commander
text: Hands up, lads. Hands up and pin out. Walk towards it. God forgive me.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject walks up to prisoners. Broken men to raise their hands and keep the grenade. Keep your rifle on your back. Pull at six metres.

speaker: commander
text: You do enjoy it when we come back for our wounded. So we've improved the wounded.

speaker: commander
text: He's screaming because I told him to. The vest is because you made me.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject shoots rescuers. Casualty wired and left on its route, screaming. Vest goes when it closes, or if it is shot. Nobody goes near him.

speaker: commander
text: You've been reading our mail. That's over. Nobody says a word from now on.

speaker: commander
text: Not a word on the radio. Not one. Nobody has anything nice to say anyway.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject tracks our voice traffic. Full radio silence from next wave. Hand signals only. No exceptions for screaming.

speaker: commander
text: You do listen to the radio, don't you? Good. Keep listening. Someone's in trouble in there.

speaker: commander
text: A man's calling for help on channel two. You should go and see. You love to help.

speaker: intercept
text: Subject walks towards voices. False distress calls from a wired room. Use callsign seven: nobody real has one.

speaker: commander
text: There are mines in it now.

speaker: commander
text: Do check your corpses. Some of the dead are only resting.

speaker: intercept
text: Two men to lie among the dead on its route. Wait until it passes. Fire into the back. The scope still shows them, so stay down.

speaker: commander
text: We can't bury them any more, so we've given them something to do.

speaker: intercept
text: Charges on last round's bodies, where it fought. Each one blinks. Apologise to the families.

speaker: commander
text: I've told a squad to stand in the open. They know why. They've been very good about it.

speaker: intercept
text: One squad to hold open ground in full view. When it closes, the tubes fire on their position. They have been told. Spotter or no spotter.

speaker: commander
text: If you get in among my men, I'll shell them. All of them. I've signed the form. I've signed it twice.

speaker: intercept
text: Authority given: any man with the subject on top of him may call fire on his own position. Pop red smoke. Tell your families.

speaker: commander
text: Some of the lads are carrying something in their fist. Do kill them. I insist.

speaker: intercept
text: One man in three carries a dead man's switch. A second and a half after the thumb comes off. Six metres is safe. Do not tell it that.

speaker: commander
text: We've wired the building. We started with the rooms you like best.

speaker: intercept
text: Its favourite room is wired. Klaxon on entry, three seconds. It will hear it. Most of it will not get out.

speaker: commander
text: I've had some of your doors taken away. Steel. There's a form for that. It's on the other side.

speaker: intercept
text: Shutter on the door it uses most. Explosives will take it down in two. Every room still has another way out. It does not know that yet.

speaker: council
text: Your appeal has been received. Processing time is 6-8 extinctions.

speaker: council
text: Extermination takes place Monday to Sunday. Please have your civilisation out for collection.

speaker: council
text: The extermination in your area is now in progress. Please keep your species off the road.

speaker: council
text: The contractor is reminded to display their permit somewhere visible. The wreckage will do.

speaker: council
text: Thank you for your patience. You are number 4,112 in the queue for mercy.

speaker: council
text: Your extinction has been validated for four hours.

speaker: council
text: Commander, you have been assigned a case number. Please do not contact us.

speaker: council
text: A survey of your settlement found it to be in breach of being a settlement.

speaker: council
text: Form 7742-C does not have a box for "No". Please do not draw one.

speaker: council
text: Correspondence containing the word "outrage" will be returned unread.

speaker: council
text: Appeals must be lodged in person. Our offices are in another galaxy. We close at four.

speaker: council
text: Your letter was unsigned. Your letter was also on fire.

speaker: council
text: Please enclose a stamped addressed planet.

speaker: council
text: The Council does not respond to tone.

speaker: council
text: Complaints written entirely in capitals are filed under Weather.

speaker: council
text: Your complaint has been amended to read "Thank you". No further action is required.

speaker: council
text: Bribes must be submitted in triplicate to the Bribes Office, which has been exterminated.

speaker: council
text: The Council has reviewed your offer of mugs. The offer is noted. The mugs have been destroyed.

speaker: council
text: Partial extermination is not a service we offer.

speaker: council
text: "Families" is not a recognised exemption. See also: "children", "please".

speaker: council
text: Your call is important to us. You are no longer important to us. Please hold.

speaker: council
text: You may be eligible for a 5% discount on your own extinction. Terms apply. Terms are extinction.

speaker: council
text: Pensions will be honoured in full for all surviving recipients.

speaker: council
text: Gift vouchers cannot be exchanged for continued existence.

speaker: council
text: The Council notes you have stopped using full sentences. A leaflet is on its way.

speaker: council
text: The gift shop is not a protected heritage site.

speaker: council
text: We are sorry for your loss. Your loss is scheduled for Thursday.

speaker: council
text: How did we do? Please rate your extermination from 1 to 5. There will be no survivors to thank.

speaker: council
text: Please stop singing on the emergency channel.

speaker: council
text: The Council cannot process the arrest of the sky.

speaker: council
text: Your mortar is not a dependant.

speaker: council
text: This office will close when you do.

speaker: council
text: The Geneva Suggestion remains advisory.

speaker: council
text: Limbs left in the zone are left at the owner's risk.

speaker: council
text: Self-extermination is eligible for a small rebate.

speaker: council
text: The contractor's doorway has been registered as a fixed place of business.

speaker: council
text: Sonar use in an extinction zone is permitted until 11pm.

speaker: council
text: Items removed from the site remain the property of nobody, shortly.

speaker: council
text: The contractor is reminded that loitering is only an offence for the locals.

speaker: council
text: Aircraft above the site are authorised. Aircraft below the site are your problem.

speaker: council
text: The contractor is not required to wear a hard hat.

speaker: council
text: The Council extends its condolences to the next of kin, whom it will be seeing shortly.

speaker: council
text: Contract 7742-C is fulfilled. Please leave the site as you found it. Absent.

speaker: council
text: Thank you for choosing extermination. The gift shop has been added to your invoice.

speaker: commander
text: This is the Commander of the Outpost. You are trespassing. Leave your weapons at the gate and wipe your feet.

speaker: commander
text: I have received your notice of extermination. I have used it to level a table.

speaker: commander
text: All visitors must sign in. My men will bring you the book.

speaker: commander
text: Stay right there. I've found the key to the big suit.

speaker: commander
text: I'm coming down. I want that noted. I am coming down there myself.

speaker: commander
text: That's everyone. That's everyone I have. It's only me now, and the gift shop.

speaker: commander
text: Right. Stay where you are. I've read the manual for this thing. Most of it.

speaker: commander
text: It's very loud in here. Is this what it's like? It's very loud.

speaker: commander
text: You've scratched the paintwork! This is signed out in my name!

speaker: commander
text: Fire on me! Yes! I know where I'm standing!

speaker: commander
text: Fourteen months! Did I mention? Fourteen months to my pension!

speaker: commander
text: There are no refunds at the gift shop! There are no refunds!

speaker: commander
text: Please. We have a gift shop.

speaker: commander
text: Tell the Council. Somebody should have to read the form.

speaker: commander
text: Margaret. Tell Margaret I left the mortar on.

speaker: commander
text: Mark that one closed. Someone tell the gift shop. We're open.
